# package tunnel

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-knx/tunnel"
```

Package tunnel is a KNXnet/IP tunnelling client over UDP: it connects to a KNXnet/IP server (an IP interface or router), sends cEMI frames with acknowledgement and retransmission, receives telegrams with sequence checking and duplicate suppression, keeps the connection alive with heartbeats and, optionally, reconnects.

The connection state machine:

	disconnected ──Dial──▶ connecting ──CONNECT_RESPONSE ok──▶ connected
	connected ──heartbeat failed / server DISCONNECT / no ACK──▶ lost
	lost ──WithReconnect──▶ reconnecting ──▶ connected (new channel)
	lost ──otherwise──▶ closed (Err reports why)
	any ──Close──▶ DISCONNECT_REQUEST ──▶ closed

One goroutine reads the socket and one sends heartbeats; both end when the Conn is closed. A Conn is safe for concurrent use; sends are serialised, as tunnelling allows one unacknowledged request at a time.

## Constants

```go
const (
	// DefaultRequestTimeout is TUNNELLING_REQUEST_TIMEOUT: the wait for a
	// TUNNELLING_ACK before the request is repeated once.
	DefaultRequestTimeout = 1 * time.Second
	// DefaultConnectTimeout is CONNECT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT.
	DefaultConnectTimeout = 10 * time.Second
	// DefaultHeartbeatInterval is how often a CONNECTIONSTATE_REQUEST is
	// sent; servers drop a connection after CONNECTION_ALIVE_TIME
	// (120 s) without one.
	DefaultHeartbeatInterval = 60 * time.Second
	// DefaultHeartbeatTimeout is CONNECTIONSTATE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT.
	DefaultHeartbeatTimeout = 10 * time.Second
	// DefaultHeartbeatAttempts is the number of connection state requests
	// sent before the connection is considered lost.
	DefaultHeartbeatAttempts = 3
	// DefaultConfirmTimeout bounds the wait for the L_Data.con of an
	// L_Data.req. The standard leaves it to the client; 3 s covers a busy
	// TP line.
	DefaultConfirmTimeout = 3 * time.Second
	// DefaultQueueSize bounds the inbound telegram queue.
	DefaultQueueSize = 256
	// DefaultSessionKeepAlive is the idle time after which a KNX IP
	// Secure session sends a SESSION_STATUS keep alive. Servers end a
	// session idle for 60 s (SESSION_TIMEOUT); 30 s leaves room for one
	// lost keep alive.
	DefaultSessionKeepAlive = 30 * time.Second
)
```

Timing constants of KNXnet/IP tunnelling (KNX Standard 3/8/4).

#### func (Conn) Receive

```go
func (c *Conn) Receive(ctx context.Context) (cemi.Frame, error)
```

Receive returns the next frame the server sent on the tunnel (L\_Data.ind, L\_Busmon.ind...), excluding the L\_Data.con of this client's own requests. It returns knx.ErrClosed, or the error the connection was lost with, once the Conn is closed and the queue empty.

#### func (Conn) Send

```go
func (c *Conn) Send(ctx context.Context, f cemi.Frame) error
```

Send sends a cEMI frame on the tunnel and waits for its acknowledgement. The request is repeated once if no TUNNELLING\_ACK arrives within the request timeout; if the second attempt fails too the connection is considered lost. For an L\_Data.req Send also waits for the L\_Data.con (unless WithConfirm(false)) and returns an error matching knx.ErrNotConfirmed if it reports an error or does not arrive.

Send never repeats a frame on its own beyond that one TUNNELLING\_REQUEST repetition. An error matching knx.ErrConnectionLost (or ErrNotConfirmed) does not tell whether the frame reached the bus: the server may have received it before the tunnel was lost. With WithReconnect the tunnel comes back on a new channel, but the frame is not resent there; the caller decides whether repeating it is safe (a read is, a toggle may not be).

### type Option

```go
type Option func(*options) error
```

Option configures a [Conn](#type-conn).

#### func WithConfirm

```go
func WithConfirm(wait bool, timeout time.Duration) Option
```

WithConfirm sets whether [Conn.Send](#func-conn-send) of an L\_Data.req waits for its L\_Data.con (default true) and how long (default 3 s).

#### func WithConnectTimeout

```go
func WithConnectTimeout(d time.Duration) Option
```

WithConnectTimeout sets the wait for a CONNECT\_RESPONSE (default 10 s).

#### func WithDeviceManagement

```go
func WithDeviceManagement() Option
```

WithDeviceManagement opens a device management connection instead of a tunnel: Send carries local device management cEMI frames (M\_PropRead.req, M\_PropWrite.req, M\_Reset.req) in DEVICE\_CONFIGURATION\_REQUESTs, and Receive returns the server's confirmations. Package devmgmt builds on it.

#### func WithHeartbeat

```go
func WithHeartbeat(interval, timeout time.Duration, attempts int) Option
```

WithHeartbeat sets the heartbeat interval, the wait for each CONNECTIONSTATE\_RESPONSE and the number of attempts before the connection is considered lost (defaults 60 s, 10 s, 3).

#### func WithIndividualAddress

```go
func WithIndividualAddress(a knx.IndividualAddress) Option
```

WithIndividualAddress requests a specific tunnelling address with the extended CRI of tunnelling v2. Servers without tunnelling v2 refuse the connection.

#### func WithLayer

```go
func WithLayer(l knxnetip.TunnelLayer) Option
```

WithLayer selects the tunnelling layer: link layer (default) or busmonitor. Raw tunnelling is not supported.

#### func WithLocalAddr

```go
func WithLocalAddr(addr string) Option
```

WithLocalAddr binds the client socket to a local address ("10.0.0.5", "10.0.0.5:3672", ":0"). By default it binds to every interface on an ephemeral port and announces the address the system routes to the server from.

#### func WithLogger

```go
func WithLogger(l knx.Logger) Option
```

WithLogger sets the logger. Logging is silent by default.

#### func WithMetrics

```go
func WithMetrics(m knx.Metrics) Option
```

WithMetrics sets the metrics callbacks.

#### func WithNAT

```go
func WithNAT(on bool) Option
```

WithNAT announces the route back endpoint 0.0.0.0:0 in the HPAIs, so that the server answers to the source of each datagram: for clients behind NAT (Docker port mappings, routers). The server must support it.

#### func WithQueueSize

```go
func WithQueueSize(n int) Option
```

WithQueueSize bounds the inbound telegram queue (default 256). When it is full, new telegrams are acknowledged and dropped (Metrics.OnDropped "queue\_full").

#### func WithReconnect

```go
func WithReconnect(min, max time.Duration) Option
```

WithReconnect makes a lost connection reconnect with exponential backoff between min and max, until the Conn is closed. Telegrams sent while reconnecting fail with knx.ErrConnectionLost.

#### func WithRequestTimeout

```go
func WithRequestTimeout(d time.Duration) Option
```

WithRequestTimeout sets the wait for a TUNNELLING\_ACK (default 1 s).

#### func WithSecure

```go
func WithSecure(c secure.Credentials) Option
```

WithSecure tunnels in a KNX IP Secure session (over TCP, or UDP with WithUDP) as the user of the credentials: the client authenticates with the user's password key and, when the credentials hold the device authentication code, verifies the server. See secure.NewCredentials and the keyring package for the credentials.

#### func WithSessionKeepAlive

```go
func WithSessionKeepAlive(d time.Duration) Option
```

WithSessionKeepAlive sets the idle time after which a KNX IP Secure session ([WithSecure](#func-withsecure)) sends a SESSION\_STATUS keep alive (default DefaultSessionKeepAlive). Servers end a session idle for 60 s, so it must stay well below that.

#### func WithStateHandler

```go
func WithStateHandler(f func(knx.State, error)) Option
```

WithStateHandler calls f on every state change, with the error that caused it (nil for a normal change). f must not block or call the Conn.

#### func WithTCP

```go
func WithTCP() Option
```

WithTCP connects over TCP (KNXnet/IP core v2, tunnelling v2) instead of UDP: no TUNNELLING\_ACKs, no NAT concerns, the connection ends when the TCP connection does. Not combinable with WithReconnect.

#### func WithUDP

```go
func WithUDP() Option
```

WithUDP tunnels over UDP: with WithSecure, the secure session runs over UDP (KNXnet/IP Secure unicast sessions) instead of TCP.
